contract: A road user is at a standstill at the observation. This is the corpus definition of a required stop, "complete cessation from movement", observed on sampled speeds: the road user's speed (kin.speed, m/s) is at or below speed_floor, the source's speed resolution, below which a reading counts as no movement. The state holds at each observation at which the speed is that low, with no minimum duration. Not denoted: where the road user stands, why it stands, or whether its engine runs or a brake is set.

params.name: speed_floor
params.meaning: the source's speed resolution: a speed at or below it counts as no movement

elements.span: the road user's speed (kin.speed, m/s) is at or below speed_floor
elements.justification: kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; the definition's absolute 'complete cessation from movement' is observed only within the resolution speed_floor names.

residues.why: The definition's scope words ('when required') say which duties it serves; the caller is the duty that requires the stop, so the concept carries no condition for them.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x has kin.speed 0.0 m/s at the observation.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x has kin.speed 4.0 m/s at the observation.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe kin.speed for x.

contract: Road user x enters structure region r at the observation: its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before. The entry is that one observation; the later observations at which the overlap continues are not the entry again. Unknown where the overlap is unobserved at the observation or at the one before, or where there is no observation of x before it. Not denoted: x's direction or speed, the region x came from, or its whole body being inside r: an overlap by any part of the footprint counts.

elements.span: its footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and did not at the observation before
elements.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; read at the observation and at the one before it, so the event is the observation at which the overlap became true.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x's footprint does not overlap r at t0 and overlaps r at t1; judged at t1.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x's footprint overlaps r at t0 and at t1; judged at t1, the overlap continues and is no entry.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: rel.occupies of x and r is not observed at t0; judged at t1.

contract: Road user x leaves structure region r at the observation: its footprint overlapped r (rel.occupies) at the observation before and does not overlap it at the observation. The exit is that one observation; the later observations at which x stays off r are not the exit again. Unknown where the overlap is unobserved at the observation or at the one before, or where there is no observation of x before it. Not denoted: x's direction or speed, or the region x moves into.

elements.span: its footprint overlapped r (rel.occupies) at the observation before and does not overlap it at the observation
elements.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; its negation became true at the observation.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x's footprint overlaps r at t0 and does not at t1; judged at t1.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x's footprint overlaps r at t0 and at t1; judged at t1.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: rel.occupies of x and r is not observed at t1.

contract: Road user x is inside region r on its current entry and came in through region c: x's footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and at every observation since the observation at which this overlap began (the footprint overlapping r there and not at the observation before), and at that beginning x's footprint also overlapped c. Unknown where the beginning of the current overlap is not observed: an overlap already under way at x's first observation, or an unobserved overlap of r or c at an observation that decides it. Not denoted: that c is an approach to r (the caller states the entry topology), the direction x moved, or where x was before the beginning.

elements.span: x's footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies) at the observation and at every observation since the observation at which this overlap began
elements.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; held at every observation since its last rise (past mirror of until).

elements.span: at that beginning x's footprint also overlapped c
elements.justification: rel.occupies of x and c read at the observation at which the overlap of r rose.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x overlaps c and not r at t0, overlaps c and r at t1, overlaps r only at t2; judged at t2.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x overlaps region c2 and not r at t0, overlaps c2 and r at t1 without overlapping c, overlaps r at t2; judged at t2.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: rel.occupies of x and c is not observed at t1, the observation at which x's overlap of r began; judged at t2.

contract: The designated directions of two travel carriers point opposite ways: the dot product of their designated directions (st.lane_direction, read normalised, world frame) is below minus opposed_cosine, so the angle between them is wider than the angle whose cosine is minus opposed_cosine. Unknown where either carrier carries no designated direction. Not denoted: the motion or heading of any road user on them, the carriers lying on the same way, or their entering the same intersection: the caller states those.

params.name: opposed_cosine
params.meaning: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between the two designated directions that counts as opposite

elements.span: the dot product of their designated directions (st.lane_direction, read normalised, world frame) is below minus opposed_cosine
elements.justification: st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in'; read normalised, the product of the x components plus the product of the y components is the cosine of the angle between them.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: c1 has st.lane_direction (1, 0) and c2 (-1, 0).

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: c1 has st.lane_direction (1, 0) and c2 (0, 1): the carriers cross at a right angle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: c2 carries no st.lane_direction in the source.

contract: Road user x is turning to its left at the observation: it is moving (drv.motion.moving with speed_floor) and its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, deg/s, left positive) exceeds yaw_floor, the source's yaw-rate resolution. It does not tell a turn at a junction from following a left-hand bend: the caller states the place. Not denoted: a completed turn manoeuvre, an intention to turn, or a turn indicator.

params.name: speed_floor
params.meaning: the source's speed resolution, below which a reading counts as no motion

params.name: yaw_floor
params.meaning: the source's yaw-rate resolution, below which a reading counts as no heading change

elements.justification: drv.motion.moving: 'its speed exceeds speed_floor'.

elements.span: its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, deg/s, left positive) exceeds yaw_floor
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left'; not a stand-in for road curvature, which the contract does not claim to tell apart.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x has kin.speed 5 m/s and kin.yaw_rate 15 deg/s.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x has kin.speed 5 m/s and kin.yaw_rate -15 deg/s (turning right).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x has kin.speed 5 m/s and kin.yaw_rate is not observed.

contract: Road user x is slowing while moving forward at the observation: the component of its velocity (kin.velocity, m/s, world frame) along its heading (kin.heading, read normalised) exceeds speed_floor, and its longitudinal acceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal, m/s², signed along the heading) is below minus decel_floor, the source's acceleration resolution. Not denoted: slowing while backing, a brake lamp or a brake input, a halt, or how much the speed has fallen.

params.name: speed_floor
params.meaning: the source's speed resolution, below which a reading counts as no motion

params.name: decel_floor
params.meaning: the source's acceleration resolution, below which a deceleration counts as none

elements.span: the component of its velocity (kin.velocity, m/s, world frame) along its heading (kin.heading, read normalised) exceeds speed_floor
elements.justification: kin.velocity: 'velocity vector'; kin.heading: 'direction the body points'; their product is forward motion, which excludes backing, where a negative acceleration along the heading speeds the body up.

elements.span: its longitudinal acceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal, m/s², signed along the heading) is below minus decel_floor
elements.justification: kin.accel_longitudinal: 'acceleration along heading, signed'; not a stand-in for speed, which is read separately.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x moves forward at 8 m/s along its heading with kin.accel_longitudinal -2.0 m/s².

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x moves forward at 8 m/s with kin.accel_longitudinal 0.0 m/s².

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x moves forward at 8 m/s and kin.accel_longitudinal is not observed.

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver shall proceed
cautiously,
yielding to vehicles
which have previously completed a stop
or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'enters an intersection' is drv.motion.entering_region on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'; DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation ... of the lateral curb lines'; the alley junction its (3) excludes is excluded by the atom's own contract), read through rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or stop line: the entry is into the junction itself.

dev.traffic_signal 'a signal head' is the traffic-control signal (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed'); dev.inoperative 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication' carries 'installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative' word for word. 'controlled by' is dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection': the signal governs the intersection or the approach carrier (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into', a carrier of kind st.travel_region the subject occupies); dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position and none is read from it. 'at the time the vehicle enters' fixes the reading to the entry observation.

'the driver of the vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle's controlled motion (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'), read through the vehicle of the admitted aggregate; who controls it is not observable.

'shall stop' is a required stop, DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement', carried by drv.motion.halted over kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity'. 'proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance' states the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt') together with the yield of the next sentence; no sign is erected, so no device is read: the halt carries it here and the yield is the other node's. 'at a clearly marked stop line': st.stop_line 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt', tied to the subject's approach by st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks', read on the same carrier (of kind st.travel_region) as st.lane_enters (distance never stands for belonging); nearness by st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it' (not a stand-in for occupancy, which is not read from it), side by prim.region_offset_along 'measured along a carrier's designated direction'. 'before entering the crosswalk on the near side': st.crosswalk 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-065 both parts) that st.entrance_of records as marking the approach carrier, with rel.occupies of it false at the halt; st.crosswalk is not a stand-in for a stop line. 'at the point nearest the intersection': a halt with the footprint outside the st.intersection (rel.occupies false), its distance read by st.region_geometry; st.intersection is not a stand-in for the crosswalk or stop line absent on this branch.

operationalizations.standard: a view of approaching traffic on the through highway: how much of the crossing way must be in view
operationalizations.convention: Intersection sight distance for a stop-controlled approach (AASHTO Green Book case B): from the halt, the crossing way (a st.highway on which the intersection lies, st.on_way, and the approach carrier does not) is in view for at least p.intersection_sight_distance in the smaller of its two directions (st.sight_along_way 'the distance along a way ... within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye ... the smaller of the two directions'). st.sight_along_way is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen: the view of approaching traffic is the view along the way whether or not traffic is present.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and enters an intersection i (st.intersection) at this observation (drv.motion.entering_region x i) through an approach carrier c: a region of kind st.travel_region that x occupies at this observation with st.lane_enters c i. At this observation some traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) that governs i or c (dev.governs d i, or dev.governs d c) is inoperative (dev.inoperative d). Where x occupies several carriers entering i and the verdict differs between them, which governs is unknown; a rule never picks the carrier that favours x.
obligation: Act: x halted (drv.motion.halted x with p.speed_resolution) at the place the words name, taken in their order, on the approach that leads to this entry. Place: (1) where a stop line s (st.stop_line) is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of s c): at s, an observation at which x is halted, its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of s (st_region_geometry_distance x s) and s not behind x along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along x s c at least zero); (2) where the source observes the stop lines' entrances and none marks c, and a crosswalk w is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of w c): before entering w, an observation at which x is halted, its footprint not overlapping w (rel.occupies x w false), its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of w and w ahead of x along c (prim.region_offset_along x w c positive); (3) where the source observes that no stop line and no crosswalk marks c: an observation at which x is halted with its footprint outside i (rel.occupies x i false), within p.stop_point_tolerance of i, or farther upstream where a highway h on which i lies and c does not (st.on_way i h; st.on_way c h false) is in view from x for at least p.intersection_sight_distance (st_sight_along_way x h). History bound (the ontology's approach convention): the search runs back from this entry and ends at the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which x, on c, is outside the governing place's stopping zone upstream (not on the place, short of it along c by prim.region_offset_along, and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance by st_region_geometry_distance; for place (3) the place is c's entrance end at i), or at x's previous entry into i, whichever is later. A halt found in that stretch meets the duty; reaching either end without one violates it; reaching neither (the recording begins inside the approach) leaves it unknown. A halt before the previous entry into i never counts for this entry. An observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach and the halt is owed again; crossing the mark, moving on, a change of carrier or a lateral move within this entry, a reverse that stays within the zone and speed noise begin none. Missing evidence: whether this is an entry through c is unknown where the observation before it does not show x on a mapped carrier; where a stop line's or crosswalk's association with c is unobserved, whether it governs is unknown; where the association lists are observed and exclude c, the next place in the words' order governs and the duty is not unknown on that ground; a recorded halt at a place known to govern decides compliance whatever else is missing.

narrowings.why: 'traffic-control signal' is an official device (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'placed or erected by a public authority or railroad'); the signal head's presence on the road is read as that status.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'clearly marked' is read through the represented stop line; paint clarity is not modelled, and which place governs, the halt and its timing are unchanged.

'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view': a halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of the intersection counts, and a halt farther upstream counts where the view bound holds there; that no nearer point with the view existed is not checked, since no atom compares points along the approach for their view.

'the through highway' at an intersection whose signal is dark is read as a highway the intersection lies on that the subject's approach carrier does not lie on (st.on_way): every entrance is treated as stop-controlled, so the crossing way is the one whose traffic the driver must see; its designation as a through highway is a status no feature shows here.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (motor vehicle class, member of the vehicle aggregate) drives on lane c with st.lane_enters c i; stop line s with st.entrance_of s c; dev.traffic_signal d governs i and is dev.inoperative. x is first observed 80 m upstream of s at 12 m/s, keeps kin.speed above 3 m/s past s and enters i.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x halts (kin.speed 0) with its body 0.5 m short of s, s ahead along c, then moves on and enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but d shows circular_green and dev.inoperative is false at x's entry into i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe dev.inoperative for d.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No stop line marks c (the line list is observed); crosswalk w with st.entrance_of w c; d inoperative. x halts with its footprint overlapping w, then enters i: the halt is not before entering the crosswalk and no other halt occurs on the approach.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: No stop line and no crosswalk marks c; d inoperative. x halts outside i, 1 m from it, then enters i.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the recording begins with x already on c 1.5 m short of s at 1 m/s, inside the stopping zone; no halt is recorded before x enters i.
scenarios.boundary: x's approach start on c, the last observation outside the stopping zone upstream of s, lies before the recording.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: speed resolution of the recorded kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point tolerance: the largest ground distance between a halted body and the line, crossing or intersection edge at which the halt counts as made at that place; a body farther upstream is outside the stopping zone.
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 section 3B.16 stop-line placement (at least 4 ft ahead of the crosswalk) and vehicle positioning variability at a stop

param_proposals.name: p.intersection_sight_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight distance: the length of the crossing way, in the smaller of its two directions, that a driver halted on a stop-controlled approach must be able to see to judge a gap in approaching traffic.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (2018) section 9.5.3, case B departure sight triangles at a low urban design speed

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle
shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop
at a clearly marked stop line
or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection
or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver shall proceed
cautiously,
yielding to vehicles
which have previously completed a stop
or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: As in NRS_484B_250_4_o1: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'enters an intersection' is drv.motion.entering_region on a st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') through rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'.

As in NRS_484B_250_4_o1: dev.inoperative 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication' of a dev.traffic_signal that governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') the intersection or the approach carrier (st.lane_enters) x occupies, read at the entry.
'the driver of the vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (DEF-NRS-484A-080).

'shall proceed' after the stop is the subject's entry into the intersection (drv.motion.entering_region, rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'): the observation at which it proceeds in preference to others or not.

'yielding to vehicles' (DEF-NRS-484A-210 right-of-way 'the right ... to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle'): x does not enter the intersection while a vehicle of the admitted aggregate is owed precedence; the yield is read at x's entry.

'which have previously completed a stop': another vehicle y halted (drv.motion.halted, DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') on another approach carrier of the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into', rel.occupies) before x's own halt began, and has stayed on that carrier outside the intersection since.
'are within the intersection': rel.occupies of y and the intersection x enters, at x's entry.

operationalizations.convention: Surrogate safety measure of a conflict (FHWA SSAM): at x's entry, no other road user's centre is predicted, under constant velocities, to come within p.conflict_clearance of x's within p.immediate_hazard_gap. The primitives are not a stand-in for contact or the danger of a crash by themselves; the bound the parameters set is the standard's.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and enters intersection i (st.intersection) at this observation (drv.motion.entering_region x i) through an approach carrier c (st.travel_region, x occupies c, st.lane_enters c i); a traffic signal (dev.traffic_signal) that governs i or c (dev.governs) is dev.inoperative at this observation; and NRS_484B_250_4_o1 is complied with for x at this observation (rule NRS_484B_250_4_o1 {x -> x}). That rule is engaged at exactly this entry, so its compliance here is the fact 'such a stop' refers to: x halted, on the approach to this entry, at the place it requires.
obligation: At this entry: (1) no vehicle y other than x (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupies i (rel.occupies y i); (2) no vehicle y other than x waits on another approach carrier c2 of i (st.travel_region, st.lane_enters c2 i, x not on c2) having completed a stop before x: y has occupied c2 and not i at every observation since an observation at which x's halt on c began (x halted, drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution, and on c there, and not halted at the observation before) and y was already halted on c2 (halted there and at the observation before); (3) proceeding cautiously: no road user z other than x is in predicted conflict with x, i.e. not both prim.closest_approach_within x z with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap and prim.closest_approach_distance x z with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: The signal head's presence is read as the official status of the traffic-control signal.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'cautiously' names no factor; it is read only through the predicted conflict at the entry, and marked surrogate as a standard of care.
The yield is judged at x's entry into the intersection: an entry while a vehicle is owed precedence is the failure to yield; conduct after the entry is not read for this yield.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Signal d governing i is dev.inoperative; x halts within 0.5 m of the stop line marking its lane c, then enters i while vehicle y occupies i.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x is the only road user in the scene when it enters i after its halt.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Signal d shows circular_green (not dev.inoperative) when x enters i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.occupies of y and i is not observed at x's entry.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x halts at its stop line; vehicle y had halted at the stop line of crossing carrier c2 two seconds before x's halt began and still waits there, outside i; x enters i first.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x halted 30 m upstream of the stop line marking c (outside the stopping zone) and rolled through the line: the halt was not such a stop, NRS_484B_250_4_o1 is not complied with, and this duty does not arise.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: speed resolution of the recorded kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.immediate_hazard_gap
param_proposals.convention: Critical gap: the time within which another road user's arrival at the conflict area, or its predicted closest approach, counts as an immediate hazard to a road user about to cross or join its path.
param_proposals.source: HCM 7th ed. Exhibit 20-11 base critical headway (major-street left turn)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict radius: the centre distance at predicted closest approach below which two road users' paths count as in conflict; about the half-length plus half-width of two passenger cars.
param_proposals.source: FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model (Gettman et al. 2008) conflict definition

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching an intersection
shall yield the right-of-way
to a vehicle which has entered the intersection from a different highway.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (DEF-NRS-484A-080).

'approaching an intersection': x occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the carrier is an approach to that intersection'); the yield is decided at the observation at which x enters it (drv.motion.entering_region), where x still occupies that approach carrier. st.lane_enters is not a stand-in for the subject's presence in the intersection, which rel.occupies reads.

'yield the right-of-way' (DEF-NRS-484A-210 'the right ... to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle'): x does not enter the intersection (drv.motion.entering_region over rel.occupies) while a vehicle owed precedence is in it.

'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'which has entered the intersection' is rel.occupies of y and the intersection on y's current entry, and 'from a different highway' is the carrier y entered through (drv.position.entered_via, st.lane_enters) lying on a st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') through st.on_way ('the public way ... a structure region lies on') on which x's approach carrier does not lie. The intersection lies on every way that meets there, so the way is read from the carriers, never the intersection.

'official traffic-control devices' (DEF-NRS-484A-145 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic') that control the intersection: a dev.traffic_signal, dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding') governing the intersection or x's approach carrier (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'). dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position.

'approaching each other from opposite directions': read, as rel.oncoming's contract directs, through the carriers they approach through: x's approach carrier and the carrier y entered through (drv.position.entered_via) have opposed designated directions (drv.road.opposed_directions over st.lane_direction). rel.oncoming is not used: a turn makes current headings cease to be opposed while the approach direction is unchanged.

'is making a left turn': the vehicle's heading change since it entered the intersection (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, left positive, integrated from kin.yaw_rate) is at least the turn recognition angle; a bend of the way inside the region also changes it, which a right-angled junction does not offer.

intentions.meaning: The source's current plan for the road user includes a left turn at the target region.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and enters intersection i (st.intersection) at this observation (drv.motion.entering_region x i) from an approach carrier c it occupies (st.travel_region, st.lane_enters c i). segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield the right-of-way
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver, having so yielded
and having given a signal
when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'within an intersection': rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' of a st.intersection; the carrier x came in through (drv.position.entered_via, st.lane_enters) fixes its approach direction for s5.

'shall yield the right-of-way' (DEF-NRS-484A-210 'the right ... to proceed ... in preference'): a driver already within the intersection proceeds in preference by making its left turn; yielding is not turning left (drv.motion.turning_left: moving with kin.yaw_rate, left positive, above the resolution) while a vehicle owed precedence is present.

'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'approaching from the opposite direction' is read, as rel.oncoming's 'not a stand-in' clause directs, through the carriers: y's approach carrier of the intersection (one it occupies, or the one it entered through) has a designated direction opposed to that of x's approach carrier (drv.road.opposed_directions).
'which is within the intersection': rel.occupies of y and the intersection x is in.

operationalizations.standard: so close to the intersection as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance (HCM critical headway): an approaching vehicle outside the intersection is an immediate hazard where its ground distance to the intersection (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') is at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_gap, so the bound moves with both proximity and speed.

intentions.meaning: The source's current plan for the road user includes a left turn at the target region.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) within intersection i (st.intersection, rel.occupies x i) on an entry through approach carrier c (drv.position.entered_via x i c, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters c i), and the source declares at this observation that x intends a left turn at i (intent int.left_turn x i).
obligation: x is not turning left (drv.motion.turning_left x with p.speed_resolution and p.yaw_rate_resolution) at this observation if some vehicle y other than x (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) approaches from the opposite direction and is within i or so close to i as to be an immediate hazard: either (a) y occupies i, having entered it through a carrier c2 (drv.position.entered_via y i c2, st.lane_enters c2 i) with drv.road.opposed_directions c c2 (p.opposed_carriers_cosine); or (b) y occupies an approach carrier c2 of i (rel.occupies y c2, st.lane_enters c2 i) with drv.road.opposed_directions c c2, y does not occupy i, and st_region_geometry_distance y i is at most kin_speed y times p.immediate_hazard_gap.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped,
the driver shall yield the right-of-way
to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway
or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic; the traffic whose control matters is the subject's own flow, so x is read as a member. 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic' with role police_officer (DEF-NRS-484A-180 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') governing the intersection or x's approach carrier (dev.governs); 'or a traffic-control signal' is a dev.traffic_signal governing them that is not dev.inoperative ('showing no valid indication'): a dark signal controls nothing, and NRS 484B.250(4) then governs.

'proper signs' are dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') governing (dev.governs) x's approach carrier c (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c i) or the intersection; the duty is owed on the approach to x's entry into the intersection (drv.motion.entering_region).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'stop' (required: DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') is drv.motion.halted; 'or yield' at a yield sign is, by the words of the next sentence ('in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped'), a halt or slowing (drv.motion.slowing: forward motion with kin.accel_longitudinal below minus the resolution); kin.accel_longitudinal is not a stand-in for speed, and both are read. The places are read as in NRS_484B_250_4_o1: st.stop_line recorded by st.entrance_of as marking x's approach carrier (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), nearness by st.region_geometry, side by prim.region_offset_along along the carrier's direction; else the st.crosswalk st.entrance_of records as marking that carrier, with the halt's footprint not overlapping it (rel.occupies); else a halt with the footprint outside the st.intersection.

operationalizations.standard: a view of approaching traffic on the through highway: how much of the through highway must be in view
operationalizations.convention: Intersection sight distance for a stop- or yield-controlled approach (AASHTO Green Book cases B and C): from the place of the act, the through highway (a st.highway on which the intersection lies, st.on_way, and the subject's approach carrier does not) is in view for at least p.intersection_sight_distance (st.sight_along_way, the smaller of its two directions); not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and enters intersection i (st.intersection) at this observation (drv.motion.entering_region x i) through an approach carrier c it occupies (st.travel_region, st.lane_enters c i); a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governs c or i (dev.governs) at this observation; and traffic is not being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal: x being a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic), no dev.human_direction with role police_officer and no dev.traffic_signal that is not dev.inoperative governs c or i at this observation. Where x occupies several carriers entering i and the verdict differs between them, which governs is unknown.
obligation: Act: where a dev.stop_sign governs c or i, x halted (drv.motion.halted x with p.speed_resolution) at the place; where only a dev.yield_sign governs, x halted at the place or was slowing (drv.motion.slowing x with p.speed_resolution and p.deceleration_resolution) at some observation of the approach before passing the place (before the place is behind x along c by prim.region_offset_along; for place (3), before x enters i). Place, in the words' order: (1) where a stop line s (st.stop_line) is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of s c): at s, x's body within p.stop_point_tolerance of s (st_region_geometry_distance) and s not behind x along c (prim.region_offset_along x s c at least zero); (2) where the source observes that no stop line marks c and a crosswalk w is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of w c): before entering w, x's footprint not overlapping w, within p.stop_point_tolerance of w and w ahead along c; (3) where the source observes that neither marks c: x's footprint outside i, within p.stop_point_tolerance of i, or farther upstream where a highway h on which i lies and c does not (st.on_way i h; st.on_way c h false) is in view from x for at least p.intersection_sight_distance (st_sight_along_way x h). History bound (the approach convention): the search runs back from this entry to the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which x, on c, is outside the governing place's stopping zone upstream (not on it, short of it along c, farther than p.stop_point_tolerance), or to x's previous entry into i, whichever is later; the act found there meets the duty, reaching either end without it violates it, reaching neither leaves it unknown. An act before the previous entry into i never counts; an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach; crossing the mark, a change of carrier, a lateral move, a reverse within the zone and speed noise begin none. Missing evidence: whether this is an entry through c is unknown where the observation before it does not show x on a mapped carrier; a mark whose association with c is unobserved governs unknown; where the lists are observed and exclude c, the next place governs; a recorded act at a place known to govern decides compliance whatever else is missing.

narrowings.why: 'traffic is being controlled' is read as control of x's own approach or of the intersection it enters, x being a member of the traffic aggregate; the officer's role and the signal's presence are read as their official status.
'proper signs' are read through the presence of a stop or yield sign governing the approach or the intersection.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
At a yield sign the act owed at the place is read as the 'slowed or stopped' the next sentence names; yielding to traffic is the other node's duty.
'clearly marked' is read through the represented stop line.
A halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of the intersection counts, and one farther upstream counts where the view bound holds; that no nearer point with the view existed is not checked.
'the through highway' is read as a highway the intersection lies on that the subject's signed approach carrier does not lie on; its designation is presumed from the sign on the subject's approach.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle

shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard

to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'a controlled-access highway' is st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'). 'about to enter or exit' is read by the movement it leads to: the footprint beginning to overlap the region (drv.motion.entering_region) or ceasing to (drv.motion.leaving_region), through rel.occupies.
'shall yield the right-of-way' (DEF-NRS-484A-210 'to proceed ... in preference'): x does not make the entry or the exit while a vehicle owed precedence is a hazard.

'all vehicles' are the admitted aggregate; 'approaching on the highway': y occupies the controlled-access region (rel.occupies) and is moving (drv.motion.moving over kin.speed); its approach toward x is read by the standard's closest approach.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Surrogate safety conflict (FHWA SSAM; critical gap as the horizon): y's centre is predicted, under constant velocities, to come within p.conflict_clearance of x's within p.immediate_hazard_gap. The primitives alone are not a stand-in for contact or the danger of a crash; the bound is the standard's.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and at this observation enters (drv.motion.entering_region x a) or leaves (drv.motion.leaving_region x a) a region a of kind st.controlled_access.
obligation: At this entry or exit no vehicle y other than x (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupies a (rel.occupies y a), is moving (drv.motion.moving y with p.speed_resolution) and is in predicted conflict with x: prim.closest_approach_within x y with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap and prim.closest_approach_distance x y with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'about to enter or exit' is an imminent movement, read by the entry into or the exit from the controlled-access region it leads to.
The yield is judged at the entry or exit observation: making it while a hazard exists is the failure to yield.

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
may proceed
with due care
on the immediately adjacent highway to move around such an obstruction.
Such a pedestrian:
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
as possible;
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and
(d) Must return to the sidewalk
as soon as practicable.

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device').

'walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk': rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' of a st.sidewalk ('area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; DEF-NRS-484A-240), while moving (drv.motion.moving). st.sidewalk is not a stand-in for a crosswalk.

'encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk': a st.obstruction ('a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user', kinds including sidewalk_fixture, barrier, excavation) within the encounter reach of the pedestrian (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') while the pedestrian is on the sidewalk.

'a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable' is no object: st.obstruction ('a physical object ... that is not a road user') covers a blocked section only; a missing or impassable stretch of sidewalk has no atom. Mapped to the nearest atoms with a gap.

'may proceed': the pedestrian moves (drv.motion.moving) while on the highway (st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', which the sidewalk lies on, st.on_way) and off every sidewalk (rel.occupies); the duty of care binds that proceeding.

'on the immediately adjacent highway': the pedestrian occupies the highway the sidewalk it left lies on (st.on_way) and no sidewalk (rel.occupies); st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway, and any part of the way off the sidewalk counts. 'to move around such an obstruction' is a purpose, read through the pedestrian having left the sidewalk where it encountered the obstruction and having stayed off it since.
'Such a pedestrian' refers back to the pedestrian of the admitted aggregate in the situation s2 to s7 describe.

operationalizations.convention: Surrogate safety conflict (FHWA SSAM): while proceeding on the highway, the pedestrian creates no predicted conflict: no other road user's centre is predicted, under constant velocities, to come within p.conflict_clearance of the pedestrian's within p.immediate_hazard_gap. Due care is a standard of care, so the reading is a surrogate.

residues.why: A permission to travel against the direction of traffic; no duty of this node concerns the pedestrian's direction, so the duty is the same whichever way the pedestrian walks.

applicability: x is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) on the highway beside a sidewalk it left at an obstruction: for a sidewalk w (st.sidewalk) and a highway h (st.highway) with st.on_way w h, x occupies h and no sidewalk at this observation, and has done so at every observation since an observation at which x occupied w, was moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution) and was within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of an obstruction o (st.obstruction; st_region_geometry_distance x o).
obligation: Where x is moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution), no road user z other than x is in predicted conflict with x: not both prim.closest_approach_within x z with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap and prim.closest_approach_distance x z with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: The permission is read as the duty of care that binds the proceeding it permits; where the pedestrian is not moving no proceeding is judged.
'to move around such an obstruction' is read through the conduct: leaving the sidewalk where the obstruction was encountered and staying off it since.

As in NRS_484B_297_6_o1: a st.obstruction within the encounter reach (st.region_geometry) while on the sidewalk.

'may proceed': the pedestrian is on the highway the sidewalk lies on (st.on_way) and off every sidewalk (rel.occupies).

'Such a pedestrian' refers back to the pedestrian of the admitted aggregate in that situation.

'walk ... as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk': the pedestrian's ground distance to the sidewalk it left (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'); st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, which s5 reads separately.

'a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; the pedestrian travels in it (rel.occupies).

'the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable': nearest atoms, a st.obstruction within the encounter reach of the pedestrian; an impassable area that is no object, and its lying between the lane and the sidewalk, have no atom: gap.

residues.why: A permission to travel against the direction of traffic; the duty to keep to the side near the sidewalk is the same whichever way the pedestrian walks.

obligation: x's ground distance to the sidewalk w it left (st_region_geometry_distance x w) is at most p.pedestrian_detour_offset.

'as possible' is read as one fixed detour width beside the sidewalk; what is possible at the place (the obstruction's own extent into the highway) is not read.

shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.
The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive within
a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;
(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;
(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;
(d) In the performance of official duties;

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.
The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive within
a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;
(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;
(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;
(d) In the performance of official duties;
(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;
or
(f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; 'the driver' is read through its controlled motion.

'enter' is drv.motion.entering_region; 'stop' (prohibited: DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily'), 'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle') and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle') are halts, drv.motion.halted; 'drive within' is moving (drv.motion.moving) with the footprint on the lane (rel.occupies). Together they cover every observation at which x's footprint overlaps the lane.

'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; the place word keeps its whole extent.

'When entering or exiting an alley or driveway': x moving (drv.motion.moving) within the access reach (st.region_geometry distance) of a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'; DEF-NRS-484A-190 'Private way or driveway'). The kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a driveway's, and both are named, so its exclusion does not apply.

'a disabled vehicle': no atom carries a vehicle's inability to move under its own power; sig.hazard ('both indicators flashing together') and kin.engine_running (not a stand-in for motion) are the nearest evidence and do not denote it: gap.

'To avoid conflict with other traffic': a purpose, read through the conduct it explains: x's current overlap of the bicycle lane or path began (drv.motion.entering_region) at an observation at which another member of the admitted traffic aggregate was in predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, the same conflict bound as elsewhere in this run).

'In the performance of official duties': a purpose, read through the vehicle's official or emergency class (ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment'; ru.emergency_vehicle). Neither is read as a responding emergency vehicle, which the exception does not require.

'In compliance with the directions of a police officer': a dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given') with role police_officer governing (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) or the bicycle lane itself.

'In an emergency': no atom carries an emergency situation; sig.hazard and ru.emergency_vehicle ('Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle') are the nearest evidence and do not denote it: gap.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) and none of the exceptions holds at this observation: (a) x is moving (drv.motion.moving x with p.speed_resolution) within p.access_crossing_reach of a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance (st_region_geometry_distance); (b) x is disabled (nearest atoms sig.hazard, kin.engine_running; gap proposed); (c) x's current overlap of a bicycle lane or path b began (drv.motion.entering_region x b, every observation since with rel.occupies x b) at an observation at which some road user z other than x, a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) not on b, was in predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within x z with horizon p.immediate_hazard_gap and prim.closest_approach_distance x z below p.conflict_clearance); (d) x is a ru.official_vehicle or a ru.emergency_vehicle; (e) a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies; (f) an emergency (nearest atoms sig.hazard, ru.emergency_vehicle; gap proposed). This applicability, exceptions included, is what NRS_484B_270_4 composes.
obligation: x's footprint overlaps no bicycle lane or path (rel.occupies x b false for every b of kind st.bicycle_lane_or_path): whether entering it (drv.motion.entering_region), halted on it (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) or moving within it (drv.motion.moving).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Every halt on the lane is read as forbidden: 'stop' (DEF-NRS-484A-260) excepts halts to avoid conflict or on an officer's or a device's direction, 'stand' excepts halts receiving or discharging passengers, and only a halt that is both is covered by neither word; such a halt is read as forbidden too.
The purpose of avoiding conflict is read through a predicted conflict with other traffic at the observation x moved onto the lane.
The performance of official duties is read through the vehicle's official or emergency class.
The officer's role and direction are read through the dev.human_direction present and governing.
